solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Remove tax

definitions.meaning: to cut something out or delete it
a duty levied on goods produced or sold at home

explanation.surface: An instruction to abolish a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for cutting out and a noun for a home-goods duty, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Powerful organisation extremely effusive about politician, Irish

indicators.note: about says those outer letters go around the next pieces
extremely picks the outermost letters of effusive

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A gushing Irish politician heads a mighty body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives EE, which 'about' wraps around MPIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A large business group or a realm under one ruler is a mighty organisation.

clue.text: Endless lawlessness: boy looking embarrassed?

indicators.note: endless says the word for lawlessness loses its final letter

parts.note: crime is lawlessness
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy blushes at the never-ending lawbreaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep red colour describes a face flushed with shame.

clue.text: Raised listening devices in quarrel

indicators.note: raised in a down clue says the word goes upwards, so it is read backwards

parts.note: taps are bugs on phone lines

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over bugging equipment being installed.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty argument or squabble is a quarrel.

clue.text: Mob I've trained for film

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are drilled into a new formation

explanation.surface: A gangster schools a mob for a movie role.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-budget second feature is a kind of film, named for the lower half of a double bill.

clue.text: Gosh, it's heading north over California! Awe-inspiring!

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise like gosh

indicators.note: heading north in a down clue means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An excited traveller exclaims at heading north over the Californian landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spiritual and mysterious inspires wonder, so the two fit loosely.

clue.text: First of all verify if guard is leading watch

indicators.note: first of all picks the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A security instruction: check whether the guard is in charge of the watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of staying awake to keep guard is a watch.

clue.text: Woman, blest, heroine to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Praise for a blessed heroine, partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, also a biblical queen, is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Rationale, it's shaky — fighting back?

indicators.note: shaky suggests the letters are unsteady and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A doubt about the reasoning behind a counter-attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 's is read as 'is', a link; 'shaky' rearranges RATIONALEIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking back at an attacker is retribution or a counter-attack.

clue.text: Confidential chatter around Vi's about-turn

indicators.note: around says the chatter word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to prate is to chatter idly

indicators.note: an about-turn faces the name the other way, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Vi is a woman's name, short for Violet

explanation.surface: Secret gossip about a woman called Vi changing her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vi's' looks possessive, but it is just the name Vi; 'Confidential' is the definition, an adjective like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe information kept secret and not shared publicly.

clue.text: Sense of place we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a site is a place or location

explanation.surface: A remark about getting a feel for a location from what is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Flower increased in value

definitions.meaning: went up in price, the past tense of a verb meaning to climb

explanation.surface: A flower that went up in price.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the garden bloom; the other is the past tense of a verb for going up.

clue.text: Nigel avoiding girl initially in valley — this girl?

indicators.note: in places the shortened name inside the valley word

parts.note: a dale is a valley, especially in northern England

indicators.note: avoiding says the name goes without the letter that follows

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word girl

explanation.surface: A man called Nigel steers clear of a girl in a valley, prompting a guess at her name.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'girl' does double duty: its first letter is dropped from the name, and with 'this' it points to the answer as a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a female first name, so it is an example of what a girl might be called.

clue.text: Break down wall — free! Goodbye!

indicators.note: break down says the letters are demolished and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A cry of liberation as a wall is demolished and the prisoner departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A parting word said when leaving is a goodbye.

clue.text: Stain in bath upset residents

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Householders are upset by a mark in the bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean the people who live in a place, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Ticket seller takes in upcoming teacher, one on holiday?

indicators.note: takes in says the seller word holds the other piece

parts.note: a tout sells tickets unofficially at a mark-up

indicators.note: upcoming in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: A ticket seller cons a teacher on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a holidaymaker is one example of a visitor; British pupils call a male teacher 'sir'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sightseer travelling for pleasure is typically someone on holiday.

clue.text: Large feline company disturbed a rug

indicators.note: disturbed says the letters are moved out of place

explanation.surface: A big cat with friends has messed up a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: A puma or mountain lion is a big wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Wanting to drop off agent, welcoming shelter

indicators.note: welcoming says the agent word takes the next piece in

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
lee is shelter from the wind

explanation.surface: A spy welcomes a tired colleague into a safe house.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling drowsy means wanting to nod off; drop off is an idiom for falling asleep.

clue.text: Welcome letter featuring this dish

indicators.note: featuring says the answer is contained within the words before it

explanation.surface: A letter of welcome that mentions a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded egg preparation is an example of a dish.

clue.text: Give statutory effect to, at heart, penal court

indicators.note: at heart takes the inner letters of penal, dropping its ends

explanation.surface: A criminal court making a law take force.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing a bill into law gives it statutory force.

clue.text: Target papal document

definitions.meaning: the centre of a dartboard or archery target
a formal edict issued by the Pope

explanation.surface: The Pope's decree as an object of criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullseye of a target and a sealed papal edict share this short word.

clue.text: Sceptical originally, regularly attempt short distance

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of sceptical
regularly picks every other letter of attempt

explanation.surface: A doubter makes repeated tries over a short way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A single pace is a very small distance.

clue.text: Dazzle, regal, recollected

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected says the letters are gathered up again in a new order

explanation.surface: Remembered royal splendour that dazzled.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe harsh bright light that blinds or overwhelms the eyes.

clue.text: Not a member of dismissed team

parts.note: a batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A player who has been sacked from the squad is no longer part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone excluded from a group stands beyond its circle, not belonging to it.

clue.text: Again gave account about time from past

parts.note: re is Latin for concerning, used in letters
old means belonging to the past

explanation.surface: Someone narrates a story about bygone days once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story a second time is to narrate it again.

clue.text: Lack of interest in a way, desultory in the end

parts.note: a path is a way or track

indicators.note: in the end picks the last letter of desultory

explanation.surface: A half-hearted, aimless attitude shown towards the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Indifference or not caring is the straight meaning of the answer.
